$comment: Machine-readable feature coverage. status: supported | restricted (supported with documented restrictions) | unsupported (compilation diagnostic) | not-applicable. Every supported/restricted entry lists executable tests as 'path#needle' (needle must occur in the file). Checked by tools/feature-matrix/check.mjs; docs/feature-matrix.md is generated from this file.

features.feature: Built-in scalars (string, boolean, int8–uint64, safeint, float32/64)

so.notes: Sized integers carry their range as minimum/maximum (Pydantic Annotated[int, Field(ge, le)]).

features.feature: Arbitrary precision (integer, numeric, decimal, decimal128), int64/uint64 extremes

go.notes: tsgo.Integer (big.Int) and tsgo.Decimal (exact text); decimal128 digits validated; float bounds compared in binary64 or exactly via big.Rat when the bound is not representable. Literals and defaults keep every digit; float literal membership (enums, literal types, unions, text parameters) is checked on the wire token before binary rounding. Exact numbers are bounded (10,000 significant digits, exponent ±10,000) so untrusted input cannot force expensive conversions. Distinct literals that TypeSpec 1.18 conflates are rejected. Option integer-type: int64 maps integer to int64 everywhere (fields, collections, unions, parameters, derived scalars); out-of-range input is rejected, out-of-range defaults and unsatisfiable bounds fail the compilation.

so.notes: integer → JSON integer; numeric/decimal rejected by default (Pydantic's Decimal schema accepts arbitrary strings); option scalar-encodings: wire maps them to JSON numbers (Annotated[Decimal, WithJsonSchema]).

features.feature: utcDateTime, offsetDateTime, plainDate, plainTime, duration

go.notes: time.Time, tsgo.Date, tsgo.TimeOfDay, tsgo.Duration (ISO 8601 components, calendar units kept).

so.notes: Only the default (RFC 3339 / ISO 8601) encodings, as Pydantic.

features.feature: bytes (base64, base64url, binary bodies)

so.notes: Rejected by default (Pydantic's default bytes form is UTF-8 text); option scalar-encodings: wire emits canonical base64/base64url string patterns.

features.feature: url, unknown, null, never

go.notes: url validated as absolute URL; unknown = json.RawMessage (well-formed JSON, verbatim); never properties must be absent.

so.notes: url/unknown produce schemas the OpenAI profile rejects (format uri, empty schema).

features.feature: Custom scalars, inherited scalar constraints

go.notes: Defined Go types; constraints of the whole scalar chain and of the property are all enforced.

so.notes: Intersected constraints; two different patterns cannot be expressed in one Pydantic field (diagnostic).

features.feature: @encode (date-time, duration, bytes, numbers as strings, delimited arrays, boolean as string)

so.notes: Default encodings only, as Pydantic; with scalar-encodings: wire also base64url bytes and @encode(string) booleans. Other encodings are rejected.

features.feature: Models, inheritance, spread, `is`

go.notes: Inheritance is flattened (base properties first).

features.feature: Template instantiations, @friendlyName

go.notes: Names concatenate template arguments (Page<Widget> → PageWidget).

so.notes: Arguments are spelled as Pydantic displays them: models, enums, scalars (sized integers as Annotated bounds), date/time types, lists, dicts, tuples, unions, recursive union aliases by name, numeric/boolean/string literals (Python repr), null and unknown. Anonymous objects and values are rejected.

features.feature: Enums, literal types, literal unions, open enums

go.notes: Closed enums reject undeclared values; `"a" | string` is open. Enums mixing string and number members are closed sum types of their literal values.

so.notes: Pydantic representation; mixed-type enums are type-less (rejected by OpenAI profiles) unless mixed-enums: typed-union splits them into typed branches.

features.feature: Arrays, records, tuples

so.notes: Records and tuples are generated as Pydantic does but rejected by the OpenAI profile.

features.feature: Optional, nullable, optional+nullable (absent / null / value)

go.notes: *T, tsgo.Nullable[T], *tsgo.Nullable[T]. Option response-unset-nullable (null for all, or a list of models and properties) writes unset optional nullable properties as null in server responses (nested values, JSON Lines and SSE included); unselected and request models, MarshalJSON and request decoding unchanged.

so.notes: Structured Outputs require every property: `a?: T` needs option optional-properties=nullable (explicit policy); `a?: T | null` maps to `T | None = None`.

features.feature: Nested and recursive models (incl. through unions)

go.notes: Required non-nullable self-containment has no finite value and is rejected.

so.notes: Recursive models and recursive named unions (TypeAliasType definitions, also mutual and through dicts), as Pydantic; a recursive reference with its own metadata is rejected in strict mode, where the SDK's transformation recurses forever.

features.feature: Undiscriminated unions, nested unions, ambiguous variants

go.notes: Documented policy: declaration order; the first variant that decodes, validates and re-encodes to JSON equivalent to the input (nested properties and exact numbers included); then the first valid; then the first decodable (Validate reports). Undeclared properties follow unknown-properties, as for plain models. Errors: the variants whose declared constants the input matches are reported (one: its own error and JSON Pointer; several: tsgo.UnionError), bounded and formatted lazily; constants never affect selection.

so.notes: anyOf with Pydantic flattening/dedup; literals grouped into one Literal[...].

features.feature: Uninhabited alternatives in nested unions and combined record indexers

go.notes: Nested null alternatives stay nullable, and never contributes no values to a union. An empty union has no decodable representation.

so.notes: The pinned Pydantic fixture projects a combined closed and typed spread to typed extras under target-profile none. OpenAI profiles reject the resulting open object.

features.feature: @discriminated unions (envelope object/none, default variant)

so.notes: envelope none: Union of the tagged variant models; envelope object: Union of synthesized <Union>_<tag> wrapper models (kind + value); a default variant becomes <Union>_Fallback with a tag-excluding string pattern (rejected when the discriminator is not a required plain string).

features.feature: @discriminator inheritance (single, nested, enum discriminators)

go.notes: <Base>Union sum type; undeclared values decode into the base model.

so.notes: A @discriminator base with derived models is a TypeAliasType union of the derived models and a <Base>_Fallback with a tag-excluding pattern; rejected when the discriminator already has a pattern or is not a required plain string.

features.feature: @encodedName (JSON, XML, form)

so.notes: Pydantic alias; titles derive from the alias; integer-like and Object.prototype names keep their declared position.

features.feature: Lifecycle visibility, context-dependent representations

go.notes: Variants per visibility via @typespec/http createMetadataInfo (WidgetRead, WidgetCreate, ...); full model for standalone use. Excluded properties are undeclared in the variant (rejected by closed models and unknown-properties: reject) unless invisible-properties: ignore accepts and discards them.

so.notes: Option visibility (Read, Create, Update, Delete, Query) keeps the properties visible in that lifecycle phase, recursively; without it, visibility is not applied and a warning is reported.

features.feature: JSON merge patch (application/merge-patch+json)

go.notes: RFC 7396 representation: optional members are absent | null | value; no defaults applied.

features.feature: Default values (scalars, enums, objects, arrays)

go.notes: ApplyDefaults: absent optional only; explicit null kept; fresh value per application.

so.notes: `default` is outside the documented OpenAI subset: option default-values (error | omit | emit, where emit is only accepted with target-profile none).

features.feature: Length, pattern, numeric bounds (inclusive/exclusive), item counts

go.notes: Patterns are ECMAScript regular expressions in Unicode mode (JSON Schema 2020-12), parsed with @eslint-community/regexpp and translated to RE2 with identical semantics (code points; \s and Unicode properties, including scripts, resolved to explicit code-point sets); lookaround, backreferences, lone surrogates, set operations and nested repetitions beyond RE2's limit are rejected.

so.notes: minItems/maxItems (and the string and number constraints) are kept for the openai profile; openai-fine-tuned reports every such keyword in the final schema as target-incompatible, it never removes one.

features.feature: Additional properties (...Record<T>, extends Record<T>)

so.notes: Generated as Pydantic does; rejected by the OpenAI profile (additionalProperties must be false).

features.feature: Closed models (...Record<never>): no properties beyond the declared ones

go.notes: The nearest indexer in the inheritance chain decides (inherited, reopened with ...Record<T>, or closed over an open base). Undeclared JSON properties are rejected whatever unknown-properties says, including visibility and merge-patch variants and union variant selection; form, query-object, XML and multipart inputs reject undeclared keys, elements, attributes and parts.

so.notes: Pydantic ConfigDict(extra="forbid"): additionalProperties: false in the model's own schema, at Pydantic's key position in both pydantic and strict modes (the SDK keeps it in place). Accepted by the OpenAI profiles.

features.feature: Separately compiled specifications sharing generated packages (external mappings)

go.notes: Options export-contract and external: mapped namespaces/types are imported (type identity) after verifying each declaration's fingerprint, the representation options and the shared runtime; missing variants and instances are generated in the consumer; mismatches are diagnosed. XML of mapped declarations is generated in the consumer; dependencies of a mapped type are bound to the same package. Dotted names map through tspconfig lists or nested objects; anonymous types are identified by declaration (containing declaration, path, template arguments, projection), not content; exporters may select any of their declarations for response nulls.

features.feature: Cross-emitter value-domain consistency (same TypeSpec, both emitters)

go.notes: Absent, null and zero survive for the tested overlapping representations with aligned policies. Binary floats can round an accepted number or reject overflow.

features.feature: Routing on net/http.ServeMux (RFC 6570 templates: simple, reserved, label, matrix, path, optional, explode, records, literal query)

go.notes: Expressions with several variables are supported for required scalar values (not with + or .); prefix modifiers when @maxLength does not exceed the prefix; fragments are never sent to servers.

features.feature: Path, query, header, cookie parameters (arrays, records, flat models in path and query, encodings)

go.notes: Nullable parameters (no wire form for null) and record/model header and cookie parameters are rejected. Flat path models use RFC 6570 key/value pairs and the declared field codecs. Nested fields, reserved expansion and exploded label expansion for models are diagnosed.

features.feature: Request/response bodies: JSON, text, binary, Http.File, multipart (model and tuple form), form-urlencoded, XML

go.notes: Multipart and form-urlencoded responses are encoded from the typed response; XML follows @typespec/xml (nullable and nested collections have no XML mapping).

features.feature: Operation-specific response variants: status codes, ranges, default, headers
Multiple media types, @sharedRoute content negotiation (406/415)
Streaming: server-sent events, JSON Lines (requests and responses)

go.notes: iter.Seq bodies, per-item flush, cancellation through the request context, lazy per-item decoding/defaults/validation; an invalid request item fails the request (400) even if the handler stopped reading; with ValidateResponses each response item is validated (500 before the first item, aborted stream after). Union-typed event variants, nested @data envelopes and text events of any type with a text codec are supported; set optional envelope fields are a runtime error (never dropped). Rejected: text events without a text codec, @data envelopes with other required properties.

features.feature: Authentication hooks (@useAuth schemes as OperationInfo.Security)

go.notes: Credential verification is application code (Authenticate hook); operations fail closed without one.

features.feature: Middleware, request/response validation, problem details, body limits, cancellation, concurrency
@server URLs and base paths

go.notes: Deployment configuration: the handler serves operation routes; mount under the server path (http.StripPrefix).

features.feature: Agreement with @typespec/openapi3 (operations, parameters, status codes)

go.notes: Latest version per spec. Checks normalized routes, parameter identity and presence, request body requirement, statuses, media and header names. Payload schemas and serialization are checked separately on selected cases. Eight literal-query operations have no reference route. The reference requires a body for two metadata-only visibility requests whose upstream scenarios specify no body.
